title: Data Loading Workflow
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Step through what pd.read_csv() does to a small CSV file, from raw text on disk to a typed DataFrame in memory, with the common error at each stage.

educational.topic: Loading CSV files with pandas read_csv
learningObjectives: Students will be able to explain, in order, the stages that turn a CSV file into a pandas DataFrame, including how the delimiter, the header row, data types, and missing values are handled.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through worked example with concrete data and an error note at each stage
keyQuestions: Why does one blank field change a whole column from int64 to float64?
What would the DataFrame look like if this file were loaded with sep=";"?
Which errors stop the load, and which let it finish with the wrong data?
commonMisconceptions: read_csv keeps every value as text (it gives each column one data type).
A blank field is stored as 0 or as an empty string (it is stored as NaN).
The DataFrame stays linked to the file (it is a copy in memory, and changing it does not change the file).
assessmentOpportunities: Students are given a five-line CSV file on paper in which one numeric column has a blank field and another numeric column contains the word unknown. They write the column names, the dtype pandas will infer for each column with a reason, and where NaN will appear.
